analysis:
Examined the following changes. ProviderLoop.swift adds two state fields: clusterUpdateDrainID and clusterUpdateDrainTask (head lines 566-569, per the patch excerpt). The supplied head unit at 1023-1294 contains no changes. ProviderLoopConfig.swift adds clusterMemberAnswersUpdateDrain, which defaults to false (head 40-43, 67, 85). ClusterServiceAgent.swift adds two path helpers for service-update.json and service-update-request.json (head 79-88). ClusterMemberUpdateSlot.swift changes only a doc comment (head 17-20). ClusterPairUpdate.swift is a new pure policy file covering the partner-state decision, timeouts, a Request with a 1h age bound, and read/write/take of the request file via ClusterSupervisionFiles.

Security relevance: this is an availability and update-coordination surface (A-018, T-043, TB-003). The new update request file is a same-UID local control input. Any same-UID process can write a fresh Request (isCurrent at line ~97) to trigger a coordinated restart or drain. That is comparable to the operator's existing powers under TB-003, so it is not a privilege gain. Partner progress is read over the cluster link; a malicious partner Mac can report gaveUp or ready, causing deferral or premature drain. Both Macs share an owner or cluster pairing, and the documented impact is limited to availability. No new release-verification logic appears here: staging and verification are delegated to ClusterPairUpdateCycle and SelfUpdater, which are not supplied. drainedHoldSeconds=900 bounds a stuck drain (fail-open to serving).

For integration, verify the following unsupplied code:
- ProviderLoop+ClusterUpdateDrain: drain admission is gated by clusterMemberAnswersUpdateDrain and the drain ID, and cannot bypass App Attest or authorization admission.
- ClusterSupervisionFiles: owner-only permissions and no-follow writes for the new files.
- How the other Mac's progress is authenticated over the link.
- That staged releases still go through signed-artifact verification (T-043, T-054).

No concrete regression is identified in the supplied code.
